newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson sues Great Western over deal.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson sues Great Western over deal.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co on Thursday said it was pursuing legal action to require Great Western Financial Corp, which earlier agreed to merge with Washington Mutual Savings Bank, to comply with its fiduciary duties and treat all offers on the same basis.

Ahmanson said it would challenge Great Western's $195 million lock-up provision with Washington Mutual, which it said was excessive and unacceptable in view of Great Western's failure even to talk with Ahmanson.
Ahmanson reaffirmed that it was fully committed to its own offer, announced February 18, to merge with Great Western.
Ahmanson said it was confident investors would view its proposal as compelling once they fully understood the differences between the two offers.
Ahmanson will hold an investment community meeting on March 10 in New York to discuss its bid.
Analysts and takeover specialists expect Ahmanson to sweeten its offer soon, possibly by next week. It now proposes to exchange 1.05 Ahmanson shares for each Great Western share.
Based on the closing price Thursday, Ahmanson's bid was worth about $6.0 billion, less than Washington Mutual's bid valuing Great Western at $6.6 billion.
Ahmanson raised questions about the credibility of the information that Washington Mutual and Great Western were using to promote the Washington Mutual bid.

"In particular, we view Washington Mutual's cost savings and revenue enhancement assertions as extremely suspect and unrealistic based upon what we believe is achievable and what has occurred in other similar transactions," Ahmanson said in a statement.
Washington Mutual said the merger with Great Western would result in five percent accretion to earnings in 1998 and 11 percent accretion in 1999.
Officials at Great Western declined comment.
